title: Man. Post. Cap. VII: PLAC — separable from condition, not from the person
pass_a_gloss: Placeus: if 'separable' means honors can go while riches remain, and affinities while nobility goes, then Adam's goods look separable too—natural light of the intellect, common notions, and the work of the law written on the heart can remain while rectitude, justice, and holiness are lost, as we know happened—and in that the similitude holds again. He grants the four heads were explained in order and that he lingered longest on the first. GAR misread him: Placeus said traitor goods can be separated from the condition under which they were received; GAR heard separated from the traitor himself or from the habit—so one thing said, another answered.
pass_b_english: PLAC. Perhaps when you say separable, you understand not only that they can be separated—so that, honors being lost, riches can remain, and nobility being lost, affinities can remain. But if it is so explained, who will not retort that Adam's goods also were separable, because the natural light of the intellect, and common notions, and the work of the law written in the hearts could remain, and yet rectitude, justice, holiness be lost—and we know it was done. And in this again the similitude holds. But when the heads of dissimilarity are explained, is nothing said of the first member? I acknowledge the four members were not so proposed by me that they were not explained one by one in order, and I confess I was longer in explaining the first. But the learned man, having read my words, seems to have had something else in mind which hindered him from both rightly contracting them and understanding them well. For he invents for me a mind very alien to mine. I said in the traitor's example that goods can be separated from the condition under which they were received; he understood that they can be separated from the traitor himself, or from the habit. And so I said one thing; he answers another.
source_text: PLAC. Forte cum separabilia dicis, intelligis non modo separari posse, ita ut scilicet, amissis honoribus, remanere possint divitiae, & amissa nobilitate, remanere possint affinitates. Quod si ita explicatur, quis non regerat, & bona Adami fuisse separabilia, quia & lumen naturale intellectus, & communes notiones, & opus legis scriptum in cordibus remanere potuit, & amitti tamen rectitudo, justitia, sanctitas — & factum esse novimus. Et in hoc iterum similitudo constat. At ubi dissimilitudinis capita explicantur, de primo membro nihil dicitur? Agnosco non ita quatuor membra a me proposita, ut non quatenus ordine singula explicata sint, & fateor me in explicando primo longiorem fuisse. Sed videtur vir doctus lectis verbis meis aliud quid mente agitasse, quod impedivit quominus ea & recte contraheret, & bene intelligeret. Mentem enim a mea valde alienam mihi affingit. Dixi in exemplo perduellis bona separari posse a conditione sub qua accepta sunt; ille intellexit separari posse ab ipso perduelli, aut a habitu. Itaque aliud dixi, ad aliud ille respondet.

choices.choice: Separable from condition ≠ from person/habit; GAR answered the wrong thing
